items.definition:
To persuade an unwilling person to do something by using force or threats
He was coerced into signing the document.

To make secret plans jointly to commit an unlawful or harmful act
They conspired to overthrow the government.

To cause (a train or tram) to leave its tracks; to obstruct (a process) by diverting it from its intended course
The sudden obstacle threatened to derail the entire project.

To distribute or provide (a service or information) to a number of people; to prepare and give out (medicine)
The machine dispenses hot and cold drinks.

to take food, drink, or another substance into the body
It's important to be careful about what you ingest.

to enjoy oneself in a lively and noisy way
They reveled in their victory all night long.

to revise or redo something
The editor asked me to rework the introduction of my essay.

to make a loud, harsh, piercing cry
The car tires screeched as it turned the corner.

to tremble convulsively, typically as a result of fear or revulsion
He shuddered at the thought of the cold water.

to make the motions of boxing without landing heavy blows; to argue
The boxers sparred for a few rounds before the main fight.

to cause (someone) to become perplexed and confused
The complex instructions completely bewildered him.

to make something inactive or inoperative
You need to deactivate your old account before creating a new one.

to shine brightly, especially with a soft, warm light
The polished silver began to gleam under the light.

to put at risk
His reckless actions could jeopardize the entire project.

to make as great as possible
We need to maximise our profits.

change form or nature
The virus can mutate rapidly.

react more strongly than necessary
Don't overreact to the news.

To make an attack or assault in return for a similar attack.
They threatened to retaliate if their demands were not met.

To awaken or stir up.
He tried to rouse his sleepy brother from bed.

to speak with involuntary repetitions
He tends to stutter when he's nervous.

to divide into smaller parts
The large plot of land was subdivided into several smaller lots.

to offer goods or services at a lower price; to weaken
The new store tried to undercut its competitors' prices.

diminish gradually in size, amount, or strength
His hopes of winning began to dwindle.

To cover with a thin protective layer.
We need to laminate these important documents.

block or hinder
A fallen tree was obstructing the road.

fill beyond capacity
The small room was overcrowded with guests.

define again or differently
The new policy will redefine the company's goals.

to relax after a period of work or tension
After a long day, I like to unwind with a good book.

to trouble or afflict (someone) in mind or body
What ails you, my friend?

to refuse to allow; reject
The referee decided to disallow the goal due to a foul.

calm or send to sleep, typically with soothing sounds or movements
The gentle rocking of the boat lulled the baby to sleep.

To subject to a penalty or punishment.
The referee decided to penalize the player for the foul.

To inquire too inquisitively into a person's private affairs; to use leverage to open or separate something.
Don't pry into my personal life.

to burn the surface of something with flame or heat
The hot iron will scorch the fabric if you leave it too long.

to ask for or try to obtain something from someone
The charity began to solicit donations from the public.

to color slightly; to imbue with a slight quality or characteristic
The sunset tinged the clouds with pink and orange.

to choose not to do or have something
She decided to abstain from alcohol for a month.

to arrange or design the movements of a dance
She was hired to choreograph the ballet performance.

to severely reduce or destroy
The disease could decimate the population if not controlled.

to sweep over something so as to surround or cover it completely
The flames quickly engulfed the old building.

to express the meaning of something written or spoken using different words
Please paraphrase the main points of the article.

to broadcast by television
The event will be telecast live from the stadium.

to tread on and crush
The crowd began to trample the flowers in the park.

to cover someone's eyes with a piece of cloth
They blindfolded him before the surprise party.

to depart from an established course or standard
We should not deviate from the original plan.

to give energy or enthusiasm to
The coffee helped to energize her for the long day ahead.

to act out without words
He mimed drinking a glass of water.

to reorganize or reassemble, especially after a setback
After the defeat, the team needed to regroup and plan their next strategy.

to repay (a person who has spent or lost money)
The company will reimburse you for your travel expenses.

to change (something) so much that it appears to be entirely new
She decided to reinvent herself after moving to a new city.

engage in a skirmish; to fight briefly or in a minor way.
The two armies skirmished before the main battle.

make or become solid, firm, or strong.
The concrete began to solidify quickly after it was poured.

frighten; unnerve.
The sudden noise spooked the horses.

die or cause to die from lack of air or inability to breathe.
The smoke caused him to suffocate.

exchange (goods or services) for other goods or services without using money
In ancient times, people would barter goods instead of using currency.

dispose of a dead person's body by burning it to ashes
Many people choose to cremate their loved ones.

convert (a coded message) into intelligible language
The spy tried to decode the secret message.

make (an action or process) happen sooner or be accomplished more quickly
We need to expedite the delivery of these urgent documents.

to make individual or distinct
Teachers try to individualize the learning experience for each student.

to confuse or puzzle
The complex instructions perplexed the new employee.

to trim or cut back
You should prune the rose bushes in the spring.

to pull back or withdraw
He had to retract his statement after new evidence emerged.

to decrease in size, extent, or power
The moon began to wane after the full moon.

to exist together or at the same time
Different cultures can coexist peacefully in one society.
